model.line: Massing only, not a reconstruction: 89 plain blocks (walls, houses, halls), a tinted patch of ground. Its houses, rows and halls are generated to the kind of place, not drawn from a plan of it: assumed (C). The switch `around=0` hides everything outside the walls.

facts.label: Name
facts.value: 朗润园 (春和园) Langrun Yuan

facts.label: What it was
facts.value: a neighbouring imperial or princely garden outside the garden walls

facts.label: In 1860
facts.value: held by 恭亲王 奕䜣 from 1851 (S1215; 1852 per S1218); no 1860 damage found

facts.label: Where
facts.value: C: between today's roads 朗润园北路 (osm way 1101010418) and 朗润园东路 (osm way 1101010416), north-east campus; its extent, a circle of 130 m, is assumed

facts.label: Note
facts.value: Earlier 傅恒 / 福隆安 1767, 福康安, 永璘 1809, 绵愍, 奕綵 to 1842 (S1215). 1916 to 载涛: Malone's 'Garden of Prince Tsai T'ao' (S02 p.218), where Xiyang Lou marbles were kept c.1930. Halls survive (致福轩 restored 1995-97, lead).

sources.text: Carroll Brown Malone, History of the Peking Summer Palaces under the Ch'ing Dynasty, Illinois Studies in the Social Sciences XIX, Urbana 1934; reprint Paragon 1966
